candidates.bug_description: EventLogWatcher.Dispose(bool disposing): `if (disposing) { StopSubscribing(); return; }` followed by unmanaged _eventsBuffer cleanup that only runs when disposing==false; no finalizer exists to ever call Dispose(false), so the native handle array is never released.
candidates.ground_truth_source: maintainer-quality bug report with exact code quoted; fix-PR linkage not confirmed within budget
candidates.frozen_guard_shape: bool method parameter (canonical disposing) -- shape matches, but see rejection
candidates.rejection_reason: C3 fails on the decisive mechanism, not the surface shape: whether the cleanup ever runs turns on finalizer call-graph reachability (does anything call Dispose(false)?), not on a caller passing a known/forwarded argument value into a guard -- P-037's call-site election grammar has nothing to elect here (there is exactly one production call site, always disposing:true). The resource kind (a raw IntPtr[] closed via a native P/Invoke call) is also not one Own.NET's IDisposable-flow model tracks at all, confounding any test. To the extent this resembles an existing Own.NET doctrine, it is the canonical-disposing/else-branch crediting rule that PR #306 already hardened (release credited only in the guard's positive/THEN branch) -- so even setting the confound aside, this is closer to C5 (a doctrine already strengthened) than to a P-037-specific gap.
